hook.line: Claude Code hits its token limit mid-task and you're stuck; here's the permanent fix.
hook.visual: Top half: Claude logo animates in over a 'claude code TOKEN LIMIT FIX' title; bottom half: presenter at a mic. A meme reaction clip cuts in at 1.2 s.

beats.what: Split frame: animated Claude logo and 'TOKEN LIMIT FIX' title over the talking presenter
Meme reaction clip (frustrated sitcom character) cut under the same title for the pain point
Full-screen chat UI with a cursor clicking send: the task that hits the limit
Zoom punch as he promises a permanent fix
Plugin one: orange app icon on black with its name typing in
Pixel-art invader icon with a 'Low usage limit' bar draining, over the presenter
Plugin two: ASCII-style 'HEADROOM' logo, then a flow diagram from user to model
Plugin three: full-screen red title card 'claude-mem'
Plugin four: terminal screenshot, then a big 'builds AI skills' title over app UI
Back to presenter full frame with a large 'PLUGINS' word on his chest for the comment keyword

why_it_works: Names a pain every Claude Code user has felt in the first sentence, with the fix promised by 4 s
Numbered list of four tools gives a clear progress map, so viewers stay to hear the last item
A new visual every 1.6 s (median shot) keeps each plugin on its own branded card
Comment keyword 'PLUGINS' shown in huge type on the last frame makes the CTA unmissable
weaknesses: Captions jump between top, middle and the split line, so the eye hunts for them
Plugin claims ('practically unlimited tokens') are asserted, never demonstrated
Music bed is loud relative to the voice
for_robert: Use a one-second meme-style reaction shot on the pain line; Fred could do that reaction himself (a frustrated fish face) instead of a borrowed sitcom clip.
